    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 22, 2026 at 12:23AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Yelp ›.

    In a recent development, on its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 5, 2026, Yelp (YELP -1.99%) announced a 1% year-over-year decline in net revenue to $371 million as weak consumer demand weighed on core advertising. While local ad budgets remain under pressure, rapid growth in artificial intelligence (AI) tools and data licensing offers a fresh path to long-term value creation. Three things management stated on the call stand out.

    Industry observers note that core ad revenue fell across both services and restaurant categories due to cautious business spending. To offset that drag, management is leaning into data licensing with technology partners and subscription software products.

    Sources indicate that restaurant operators and home service professionals are adopting automated voice technology to handle calls and convert customer leads. Yelp Host, the company's internal call-answering tool, expanded rapidly after integrating advanced conversational models.

    Management reduced diluted shares outstanding by 15% year over year after buying back $200 million of stock in 2026. It paused the repurchase program in the third quarter to pay down its revolving credit facility before resuming in 2027.

    Local advertising headwinds show no signs of immediate relief, with persistent inflation and high labor costs weighing on business ad budgets. Yelp relies on structural advantages like high-intent search traffic and deep partnerships with leading technology platforms to preserve engagement.

    Management is watching key operating themes, including pricing discipline in paid project acquisition and cost control around stock-based compensation (SBC).

    The broader strategy hinges on transforming search interactions into automated lead conversions across services and dining. Long-term returns depend on whether software revenue can outpace macro softness in local advertising.

    The 2 ETFs I'd Buy Today: 1 for Growth, 1 for Dividends

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (885 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Vanguard Morningstar Growth ETF ›.
    • In the last seven weeks, two low-cost stock funds have moved in opposite directions.
    • In a recent development, the Vanguard Morningstar Growth ETF (VUG -5.32%) closed Oct.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 22, 2026 at 12:37AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Vanguard Morningstar Growth ETF ›.

    In the last seven weeks, two low-cost stock funds have moved in opposite directions.

    In a recent development, the Vanguard Morningstar Growth ETF (VUG -5.32%) closed Oct. 6 at a record $92.64. As of this writing, it trades near $76, about 18% under that high. The Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD -0.76%), meanwhile, is up about 3% since Oct. 6 and is within about 6% of its own record.

    It has been revealed that that split is a major reason I like owning these two funds together. The growth fund holds many of the fastest-growing large businesses in the U.S., while the dividend fund pays a yield over eight times the growth fund's. And when one has a rough patch, the other has tended to hold up better.

    Sources indicate that the growth fund tracks the Morningstar US Large Cap Growth Index, and it owned 135 stocks at the end of September. At the time, Nvidia, Apple, Microsoft, and Alphabet accounted for about 45% of the fund's assets.

    It has been revealed that technology stocks make up about 69% of the fund by Vanguard's classification. But it's not just a tech fund. Its 10 biggest holdings also include Amazon and Tesla, and consumer discretionary stocks are around 13% of the portfolio.

    According to recent reports, what investors get for that concentration is growth. By Vanguard's measure, the fund's current stocks grew their earnings around 33% a year on average in the last five years, and the fund was valued at about 29 times earnings at the end of October. Its share price has dropped about 11% since then, so that valuation arguably looks more reasonable now. In the 10 years through Sept. 30, the fund returned around 18% a year. What's more, its 0.03% expense ratio means just $3 in yearly costs per $10,000 invested.

    NYSEMKT · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Sure, that sort of growth can come with bigger drops. The fund lost around 33% in 2022, counting dividends.

    Its 30-day SEC yield (a standardized gauge of the income a fund earns) is also just 0.37%. Put another way, dividends don't do much to cushion a fall like the current one.

    I wouldn't bet on a quick bounce. But I think 10 years is long enough for companies that have grown this fast to grow into their prices.

    Industry observers note that schwab's fund tracks the Dow Jones U.S. Dividend 100 Index, which chooses dividend payers using financial ratios meant to point to the quality and sustainability of their payouts. It owned 102 stocks as of Nov. 19.

    According to recent reports, its biggest holdings were Procter & Gamble, Texas Instruments, Coca-Cola, and Home Depot, all between around 4% and 5% of the fund. The mix looks almost nothing like the growth fund's. Consumer staples, healthcare, and energy stocks made up around 55% of the portfolio in Schwab's newest breakdown, but information technology was about 12%.

    Industry observers note that income is the top reason to own it. Its 30-day SEC yield was 3.18% as of Nov. 18, and it costs 0.06% a year, or $6 per $10,000.

    NYSEMKT · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Schwab, meanwhile, put the fund's holdings at around 18.5 times earnings at the end of October, well under the growth fund's 29 times earnings (but the two companies might calculate the number a bit differently).

    Industry observers note that this fund won't keep up when growth stocks are running, though. It returned around 12% a year in the decade ending Sept. 30, versus about 18% for the growth fund. Its dividend growth has also cooled. The last four quarterly distributions total around $1.05 a share, only about 2% more than the four before them.

    The two funds' best and worst years haven't matched up. In 2022, the growth fund fell around 33% but the dividend fund lost only about 3%, including dividends. The next year flipped that, with the growth fund returning about 47% in 2023 and the dividend fund about 5%. And since Oct. 6 this year, the growth fund has slid around 18% but the dividend fund has risen about 3%.

    Someone dividing $10,000 equally between them would pay about $4.50 a year in fund costs and earn a combined yield of around 1.8%.

    Over the next decade, I'd expect the growth fund to do most of the heavy lifting on returns, but likely not at its 18% yearly rate of the last decade. The dividend fund's job is to keep cash coming and hold up when growth stocks sell off, the way they have since October.

    I'd consider buying both funds today. And with the growth fund around 18% off its record, it's the one I'd add to first.

    #96626. What's Behind Grail Stock's Wild Ride in 2026, and What Can Investors Expect in 2027?

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (791 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    What's Behind Grail Stock's Wild Ride in 2026, and What Can Investors Expect in 2027?

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (791 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Grail (GRAL -5.33%) stock has been highly volatile in 2026, and that trend looks set to continue next year as well.
    • According to recent reports, the firm finalized its pre-market approval submission for Galleri in late January, only to follow up with disappointing top-line results from its landmark three-year trial of Galleri with England's National Health Service (NHS).
    • Industry observers note that the principle was that Galleri would detect cancers at an early stage (I and II), leading to less expensive, less intrusive, and more comfortable treatments and, ultimately, better patient outcomes.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Lee Samaha – Nov 22, 2026 at 1:07AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Grail ›.

    Grail (GRAL -5.33%) stock has been highly volatile in 2026, and that trend looks set to continue next year as well. Management expects its multi-cancer early detection (MCED) test, Galleri, to be approved in the first quarter of 2027, but that's only part of the story. Here's what investors need to know and where the stock could be heading next year.

    According to recent reports, the firm finalized its pre-market approval submission for Galleri in late January, only to follow up with disappointing top-line results from its landmark three-year trial of Galleri with England's National Health Service (NHS). The trial failed to meet its primary endpoint of a statistically significant reduction in the diagnosis of late-stage (III and IV) cancers in a population of 142,000.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Industry observers note that the principle was that Galleri would detect cancers at an early stage (I and II), leading to less expensive, less intrusive, and more comfortable treatments and, ultimately, better patient outcomes. The trial's overall failure obviously raised concerns about FDA approval and, more importantly, insurer coverage of the test. That's the crash you can see in the stock in February.

    While the trial's result was disappointing across the more than 50 cancers it tests for, it did demonstrate more compelling data across the 12 most deadly cancers (including anus, bladder, colorectal, head and neck, lung, ovary, pancreas, and stomach) that cause two-thirds of the deaths in the U.S.

    According to recent reports, as such, management continued to build the case that the Galleri test data were compelling enough to convince the FDA to approve the test and spur insurer adoption. It's a case that management highlighted at the American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) meeting at the end of May, when outlining both the NHS trial and a smaller 35,000-patient trial in the U.S. and Canada.

    The stock then soared in September after an FDA panel voted in favor of Galleri's safety, effectiveness, and benefit, paving the way for FDA marketing approval in 2027.

    Sources indicate that the ultimate adoption of Galleri by insurers and medical bodies relies on a somewhat complex set of factors and criteria that don't lend themselves to a binary assessment of trial results. For example, a medical insurer is highly likely to conduct a cost-benefit analysis, weighing the benefits of early detection against the test's cost relative to alternative tests and the cost of false positives.

    False positives not only cause significant and unnecessary stress in a patient population, but they also create unnecessary costs, as the positively tested patients will undergo more costly and specific diagnostic testing to determine whether they have cancer with a higher degree of accuracy.

    It has been revealed that readers interested in more detail on such matters can read an analysis of the two Galleri trial results in a previous article. Suffice it to say that it isn't simply a matter of the FDA approving the Galleri test and insurers adopting it en masse; the test also needs to demonstrate its commercial viability to insurers.

    In addition, management has high hopes that Medicare will reimburse Galleri under the Nancy Sewell ACT, which allows coverage and payment for FDA-approved MCED tests if the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) "determines such coverage is appropriate.".

    Management is in contact with the CMS and expects it to initiate a National Coverage Analysis (NCA) following FDA approval (hopefully in early 2027), culminating in a National Coverage Determination (NCD) about a year later.

    According to recent reports, therefore, the sequence of events next year is FDA approval, which then opens up more detailed conversations with commercial payers and insurers, and initiation of an NCA by the CMS. Ultimately, the key to Grail and Galleri's future may not be commercial payers' decision to adopt the test; it may come down to the price they are willing to pay for it. Grail's management thinks the Galleri test will ultimately settle in a $500 to $600 range, with Wall Street analysts modeling $574 in 2029.

    That would be a favorable outcome for Grail, but there's a long way to go before it takes place, and the first step is FDA approval.

    By John Ballard – Nov 22, 2026 at 1:34AM EST.

    According to recent reports, 10 stocks we like better than e.l.f. Beauty ›.

    Sources indicate that e.l.f. Beauty (ELF -5.01%) has been on a tear. This top cosmetics stock closed at $111.21 on Nov. 17, up 53% from a year earlier.

    After a run like that, investors might be hesitant to buy it in fear of buying at the top before a pullback. But the best reason to buy it is the business's momentum in a challenging consumer spending environment.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    According to recent reports, e.l.f. just posted its 31st straight quarter of net sales growth. Net sales jumped 51% year over year in the September-ended quarter. Sales were inflated by the addition of Rhode, the beauty brand e.l.f. bought in August 2025. Excluding Rhode, sales grew about 35% year over year.

    Recent findings suggest that management expects the strong results to continue. "With this momentum, we are raising our full-year net sales guidance to 22% to 24%," CEO Tarang Amin said. This works out to organic growth — which excludes the impact of acquisitions — of 9% to 11% for the fiscal year, up from the previous guidance of 6% to 7%.

    Industry observers note that the risk is that e.l.f. relies on a small number of retailers for a large share of its sales. It sells affordable makeup and skin care through retailers such as Target, Walmart, and Amazon. A loss of just one major store that sells its brands could dent the company's sales and momentum.

    According to recent reports, still, the stock looks reasonably priced. It trades at about 27 times next year's consensus earnings estimate, while analysts expect earnings to grow about 15% a year over the next several years. That's a premium, but analysts have raised their long-term growth estimates for this company that has grown sales for nearly eight years straight.

    I believe patient investors buying today could be well rewarded, especially as Amin believes the organization is in the "early days of international expansion.".

    Health insurer UnitedHealth delivered better-than-expected results for the third quarter of 2026. The company also raised its full-year earnings outlook, reflecting continued progress on its turnaround strategy.

    Following the Q3 print, Morgan Stanley analyst Erin Wright reiterated a buy rating on UNH stock with a price target of $529. "UNH's beat & raise reinforces turnaround momentum, with improving MA [Medicare Advantage]/Optum Health supporting a higher '26 EPS baseline & upside to '27 consensus," remarked Wright.

    Sources indicate that the five-star analyst added that better-than-expected performance in the UnitedHealthcare and Optum Health businesses supported another upgrade to the company's 2026 adjusted earnings per share outlook to at least $20.50. Wright noted that UNH raised the earnings guidance despite incremental investments planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.

    Furthermore, Wright highlighted management's view that the consensus 2027 EPS of $22.63 was too conservative. Reaching even the low end of the company's 13% to 16% long-term EPS growth target would imply an EPS of $23.17.

    Wright raised her 2026 EPS estimate to $20.65 from $19.82 and 2027 EPS to $23.24 from $22.54, reflecting the latest upside and an improving 2026 medical loss ratio to 87.4% from 88.1%. Overall, she believes that UNH's operational performance continues to improve, increasing her confidence in its UHC strategy and Optum Health turnaround execution.

    In a recent development, social media giant Meta Platforms has been making headlines since the launch of its Muse AI agent, which is seeing solid traction. Investors look forward to updates on the organization's AI strategy when it reveals its third-quarter results on Oct. 21.

    Heading into Q3 earnings, Guggenheim analyst Michael Morris maintained a buy rating on Meta stock and increased his price target to $850 from $700, reflecting higher estimates for 2027. He expects Muse usage momentum and engagement levels to shape investor sentiment into the Q3 earnings call.

    According to recent reports, specifically, Morris highlighted that, according to Apptopia, Muse reached 1.3 million daily active owners in five weeks versus 300,000 in the first week. Given that Muse's current adoption represents less than 0.05% of Meta's 3.6 billion daily active user base, the analyst expects management to prioritize boosting usage over near-term monetization.

    Recent findings suggest that "Over time, we believe Muse monetizes primarily through businesses paying to reach consumers through their agents, consistent with the economics of Meta's core advertising business, rather than consumer wallets," mentioned the five-star analyst. He added that the checkout integrations with Shopify and PayPal reflect this framework.

    While there are concerns that a rival could overtake Muse or the recently launched Muse Wonder and push Meta into a prolonged cycle of overinvestment, Morris remains bullish due to the firm's strong record in scaling WhatsApp and competing strongly with TikTok via Reels as well as free distribution to an extensive user base.

    After hosting a non-deal roadshow with Marvell's senior management following the Investor Day, Stifel analyst Tore Svanberg reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $370.

    According to recent reports, the five-star analyst noted that a major focus of the roadshow was the XPU and XPU Attach mix, as Marvell's Custom business expands toward its FY31 revenue target of $30 billion. In this regard, management reiterated that it expects a balanced mix of XPU and XPU Attach revenue in FY31, though it noted that either segment could grow rapidly enough to shift the mix toward 60/40 or 40/60.

    While XPU drove most of the nearly $1.5 billion Custom revenue in FY26, Svanberg expects Marvell's XPU Attach business to grow substantially through the end of the decade, leading to a more balanced mix in this business. At the Investor Day event, the manufacturer raised its FY29 Custom target from more than $10 billion to over $12 billion, mainly driven by strength in the XPU Attach business.

    In a recent development, svanberg said that another key topic in the roadshow was whether Marvell can secure enough capacity to meet its raised targets. Management said that it met with suppliers ahead of Investor Day to share its five-year goals and received commitments to support these targets. The analyst believes that Marvell's supply chain commitments give it a competitive edge over rivals as customers seek reliable partners for large-scale infrastructure buildouts.

    • In itself, buying a Cybercab right now is hardly an attractive option for most people.
    • However, they will obviously attract Tesla enthusiasts, social media influencers, and those confident in widespread regulatory approvals for Tesla's robotaxi service.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Lee Samaha – Nov 22, 2026 at 2:05AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Tesla ›.

    Industry observers note that the news that Tesla(TSLA -7.64%)is inviting select customers to buy Cybercabs isn't a game changer from a financial perspective (at least not immediately). Still, it is highly symbolic and highlights the case for Tesla shareholders holding fire on agreeing to a potential merger with Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -7.69%) (or SpaceX for short). Here's why.

    In itself, buying a Cybercab right now is hardly an attractive option for most people. They are reported to cost $29,990, but they can't be used without a $299 monthly subscription, they lack manual driving controls (a steering wheel, pedals, etc.), and they can only operate in the limited geo-fenced areas where the robotaxi service at the moment operates.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    However, they will obviously attract Tesla enthusiasts, social media influencers, and those confident in widespread regulatory approvals for Tesla's robotaxi service. To be clear, as management is, it's focused on becoming a transportation-as-a-service company with the "vast majority of the Cybercab stuff will be essentially Tesla-owned and Transport-as-a-Service," according to CEO Elon Musk.

    According to recent reports, the reality is their sale is more about generating promotional buzz around robotaxis as the company prepares for a widespread expansion in 2027. Fortunately, everything points to a quantum leap in the robotaxi rollout next year. The company continues to develop its next major upgrade of its full self-driving software, namely v15, which should be validated and released by early 2027.

    Also, Cybercab production is ramping up, and Tesla says it's gathering data on unsupervised miles with its robotaxi at a double-digit weekly growth rate.

    Sources indicate that after years of delays and missed timelines, everything points to Tesla finally releasing value from its robotaxi service next year. At which point, its investors are entitled to ask whether it would make sense to agree to a merger with SpaceX before the robotaxi ramps up.

    While an offer is not on the table, and investors don't know the terms of a deal, or whether there will even be one, it's hard not to think that a robotaxi ramp-up in 2027 would increase Tesla's share price.

    According to recent reports, as such, if you believe Tesla is undervalued right now, then anything other than a significant cash premium from SpaceX would make sense. The following table outlines the matter from a Tesla shareholder's perspective. If you are in conditions A or B (a highly unlikely scenario), you don't want to sell undervalued Tesla stock at a discount. Investors shouldn't hold Tesla stock if they believe it's overvalued, as in C and D.

    Data source: Author's analysis.

    Industry observers note that the only caveat to this table is that investors believe a united organization -- SpaceX's artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure combined with Tesla's physical AI -- would be much stronger than the sum of its parts. That argument holds merit, but it holds even more merit after te automaker successfully ramps up its robotaxi and develops the Cybercab service. The company would be in a stronger negotiating position then, and the Cybercab sales launch helps underline how close the company is to getting there.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, global stock markets remain volatile amid persistent geopolitical tensions and concerns about the sustainability of AI trade. Given this backdrop, investors seeking steady income can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios.

    Tracking recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick attractive stocks, as these experts assess a firm's ability to pay dividends consistently.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Integrated oil and gas giant Chevron (CVX) is a dividend king. The firm has increased its dividend for 39 consecutive years. At a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share (annualized dividend of $7.12 per share), CVX offers a yield of 3.14%. Chevron will announce its third-quarter results on October 30.

    In an earnings preview note on U.S. oil majors, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Chevron with a price target of $241. The analyst is focused on the tech giant's international growth prospects across Latin America, the Middle East, West Africa, and the Eastern Mediterranean.

    Sources indicate that specifically, Mehta highlighted management's commentary on solid execution in Venezuela, with gross production expected to more than double to nearly 600 kbd (kilo barrels per day) by 2031 via three joint ventures. He also noted a recent oil and gas condensate discovery in offshore Angola and is awaiting commercial updates on the West Qurna 2 and Nasiriyah projects in Iraq.

    Furthermore, Mehta expects CVX to report improved productivity and capital efficiency across domestic shale assets. He expects the improvement mainly in the Permian Basin, where Chevron projects advanced chemical treatments to drive about a 10% recovery uplift in newly introduced wells and bring down capital spend per barrel by about 25% year-over-year. Overall, Mehta expects Chevron to report Q3 2026 EPS of $4.95, above the consensus of $4.89.

    #96612. Mortgage Rates Have Jumped More Than 1 Point Since February. Home Depot and Lowe’s Shareholders Are Feeling the Pain.

    Mortgage Rates Have Jumped More Than 1 Point Since February. Home Depot and Lowe’s Shareholders Are Feeling the Pain.

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (804 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, about nine months ago in mid-February, the average 30-year fixed rate mortgage was at 6.09%.
    • Recent findings suggest that today, the 30-year fixed rate mortgage is at 7.11%.
    • In October, existing housing sales dipped to their lowest level in 16 years.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Neil Patel – Nov 22, 2026 at 2:23AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Home Depot ›.

    In a recent development, about nine months ago in mid-February, the average 30-year fixed rate mortgage was at 6.09%. At that time, it was much higher compared to what consumers saw from 2009 to 2022. Things have only gotten tighter throughout this year.

    Recent findings suggest that today, the 30-year fixed rate mortgage is at 7.11%. It has moved up more than one percentage point in roughly nine months. Outside of the past four years, it hasn't been this elevated since 2002. On a $500,000 house, the difference between 7.11% and 6.09% translates to hundreds of dollars more in monthly payments.

    In October, existing housing sales dipped to their lowest level in 16 years. This is a frozen market. And shareholders in Home Depot (HD +0.70%) and Lowe's (LOW +0.78%) are feeling the pain.

    Industry observers note that deciding to tackle a home renovation, upgrade, or repair is no small undertaking. It can be a sizable capital commitment for people. Anytime consumers deal with substantial purchases, the companies involved are exposed to fluctuating demand. Unlike buying products or services on a recurring schedule, these households can choose to delay these projects.

    With the 30-year fixed-rate mortgage above 7%, Home Depot and Lowe's are in a bind. "Housing turnover hasn't moved in four years now," incoming Home Depot chief executive officer (and current chief financial officer) Richard McPhail said on the Q3 2026 earnings call.

    Less activity in the housing market means fewer people are moving. On the flip side, when more people are changing homes, it can naturally lead to higher demand for the things that Home Depot and Lowe's sell.

    During its fiscal 2026 third quarter (ended Nov. 1), Home Depot, which is the clear leader in the industry, posted a 0.5% decline in comparable transactions. Lowe's fared worse. It reported that this figure fell by 1.7%.

    Recent findings suggest that transaction counts are a proxy for foot traffic. When it comes to any retailer, investors want to see this metric growing.

    Same-store sales (SSS), however, grew for both companies thanks to the impact of higher average ticket sizes. Both of these leadership teams called out appliances as a strong product category, pushing substantial-ticket comp sales up mid-single digits.

    Recent findings suggest that it doesn't look like these companies will get any relief soon on the macro front. According to CME Group's (CME +0.41%) FedWatch, trading activity suggests that there's a 100% probability the fed funds rate will be higher after the December meeting, up from the current range of 3.75% to 4%. The problem is inflation that's lingering longer than expected.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    It has been revealed that for what it's worth, Home Depot and Lowe's do expect SSS to be positive for fiscal 2026. And both are finding that demand from their professional customer bases, which consist of contractors, plumbers, electricians, and the like, is stronger than spending from DIY consumers. These companies are getting better at serving their professionals, enhancing areas like fulfillment, customer service, and loyalty programs.

    Past investments in supply chain and omnichannel capabilities are also paying off. Home Depot's online comparable sales jumped 13% in the third quarter. Lowe's saw a 17% gain. Their scale, supported by massive revenue bases, give them the ability to bolster their operations, which is something smaller rivals can't do.

    It has been revealed that A housing market recovery could take time, but there appears to be meaningful pent-up demand. Accessible home equity is at a record $13 trillion.

    Investors in these two retail stocks will still have to stay extremely patient, as they have been in recent years. Shares in Home Depot and Lowe's put up total returns of 19% and 16%, respectively, in the past three years. That's worse than the 69% total return of the S&P 500 index(^GSPC -3.70%).

    As long as SSS remain under pressure for these businesses, reporting strong earnings growth is out of the question. Usually a notable tailwind, it won't play much of a factor in portfolios.

    Sources indicate that on a positive note, Home Depot and Lowe's are quality companies that are on solid financial footing. They can weather the storm. Investors have to figure out, however, if they're willing to wait for the situation to improve.

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) fell 2.7% in the week that ended Nov.
    • The biggest volatility came following the November 3rd midterm elections, and it has a lot of people wondering whether now is the time to get a bit more defensive heading into 2027.
    • It has been revealed that but history suggests that this is the time to buy.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By David Dierking – Nov 22, 2026 at 3:00AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    Sources indicate that the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) fell 2.7% in the week that ended Nov. 6, its worst week since the tariff sell-off in April 2025. That was the tail end of a four-week losing streak that has helped push the index more than 6% below its all-time high.

    The biggest volatility came following the November 3rd midterm elections, and it has a lot of people wondering whether now is the time to get a bit more defensive heading into 2027.

    It has been revealed that but history suggests that this is the time to buy. In fact, it's one of the strongest track records out there.

    It has been revealed that since 1970, there have been 14 midterm elections, defined as the halfway point of the 4-year presidential term. And in each one of those midterms, the S&P 500 has been higher both 6 months later and one year later all 14 times.

    The returns for stocks have been fantastic during these periods too. The median 6-month gain post-midterm was 12.6%, more than triple that of the 4% median return during non-midterm years.

    Over the full subsequent year, the outperformance is a little more muted. Midterm years have seen a median gain of about 11% compared to 10% in other years.

    What's also impressive is that these post-midterm rallies occurred even during years when it looked like conditions wouldn't favor it. In 1974, for example, the S&P 500 was down 23% for the year at this point and rallied 21% over the next six months. In 2022, the index was in a bear market, down 16%, and still gained 3.3% over the next six months and 10.6% over the next year.

    Data source: Investing.com and the author's analysis of S&P 500 daily closing prices. Each starting point is the final close of the week ending between Nov. 7 and Nov. 13. Six months = 26 weeks; 12 months = 52 weeks.

    Admittedly, this is a small sample size so we don't want to put too much weight into these conclusions.

    It has been revealed that in the 2000s, the midterm outperformance trend has weakened considerably. While it's still maintaining its perfect record of gains, the S&P 500's performance has been pretty average overall. In most cases, the markets saw an immediate boost once the uncertainty over the election results was lifted. But beyond that, the market in recent years hasn't gotten much of an extended boost.

    As of November 17, the S&P 500 is down around 3% since election day but still up about 7% on the year as a whole.

    Sources indicate that the big question facing the markets right now is what's going to happen with artificial intelligence (AI)? Heavy spending in AI development is being viewed negatively; there could be a significant slowdown in data center development; and worries are growing that red-hot earnings growth rates are ready to slow.

    Above average inflation, high interest rates, and the potential for multiple Fed rate hikes over the next several quarters could also pose headwinds.

    Earnings growth for the S&P 500 is still expected to be solid, but there are any number of factors that could, over the next 12 months, derail the narrative.

    The high degree of uncertainty looking forward over the next few quarters helps make the case for a long-term view.

    History is on the side of the S&P 500 here, but investor confidence has been shaken over the past month, and the number of potential stumbling blocks is getting major. This could very well be the year the post-midterm bounce trend doesn't hold.

    Since the markets could move in either direction, the best idea is probably to just stay put. Don't try to time the market and bet which way stock prices will move. Just keep contributing to your accounts and maintain a focus on your goals further down the road instead.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 22, 2026 at 3:30AM EST.
    • 10 stocks we like better than Advanced Micro Devices ›.
    • Chip stocks can't seem to catch a break.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 22, 2026 at 3:30AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Advanced Micro Devices ›.

    Chip stocks can't seem to catch a break. Recent developments, including a scandal and a major leadership change at Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%), the most important semiconductor company, have weighed on the industry.

    Recent findings suggest that another market leader is now facing a headwind. Advanced Micro Devices (AMD -13.25%) was the target of a short-seller report published on Nov. 19, which sent the company's shares down significantly, extending the losses the chipmaker had experienced over the past few weeks. Is AMD worth investing in on the dip?

    It has been revealed that hunterbrook Media, an investigative journalism outlet, published the report in question. It is affiliated with Hunterbrook Capital, a hedge fund that trades based on reporting from its journalism arm.

    In the report, Hunterbrook claims that some of AMD's firmware ended up in the hands of a Chinese server manufacturer that the U.S. government has blacklisted. That means AMD cannot sell its software to this tech giant, at least not without the appropriate license or authorization, and may be in violation of export restrictions if it does so.

    According to recent reports, if AMD is found to have broken the law, it could face penalties, including a hefty fine, more stringent export restrictions, or, worse, criminal investigations involving its executives. This could disrupt the tech giant's business for a while.

    It has been revealed that but that's if the allegations are true. Hunterbrook itself acknowledges that it doesn't know how this Chinese organization got hold of AMD's firmware. It could have obtained the firmware in various ways that do not involve the company that made it.

    Recent findings suggest that there's also the possibility that AMD does have the appropriate export license. At any rate, there is limited direct evidence that demonstrates wrongdoing on the part of AMD, at least in my view.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    It has been revealed that it's worth noting that AMD has denied these allegations. That's what the tech giant would do, of course. It wouldn't simply acknowledge wrongdoing publicly. However, Hunterbrook Capital itself stands to gain from a decline in AMD's stock price.

    That's how short-sellers make money. So there is also a financial incentive. Meanwhile, Reuters, a highly respected journalism outlet, remarked that it could not independently verify Hunterbrook's claims. That doesn't mean the claims are false.

    But the evidence for them is looking slim, at best. In my view, investors should ignore this whole debacle and continue focusing on AMD's fundamentals and business outlook. And once we do that, there is a strong case for investing in AMD.

    Industry observers note that consider the manufacturer's third-quarter results. AMD's revenue increased by 45% year over year to $13.4 billion. The company's non-GAAP gross margin was 56%, up from 54% in the year-ago period, while it posted non-GAAP earnings per share of $2.09, up 74% from the prior-year quarter.

    AMD's data center segment was once again the star of the show, with its sales nearly doubling to a record $8.5 billion. Business is booming for AMD, and there is more where that came from. The tech giant's leadership in CPUs (central processing units) positions it well to capitalize on the growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) agents.

    Agentic AI runs on CPUs, and this market is driving up AMD's sales. As management noted, data center revenue growth has accelerated every quarter this year, and that should continue in the fourth quarter, thanks in part to the ongoing agentic AI boom. AMD expects revenue growth of more than 80% in 2027, well above the growth it posted in 2026.

    And over the next five years, we could see the semiconductor leader continue to tap into its large server CPU total addressable market (TAM), which should reach $220 billion by 2030, according to the company's projections -- and AMD has increased its mid-term TAM estimates several times over the past year as demand for its products continues to expand.

    The opportunity across the entire range of its business is even larger. Lastly, AMD is trading at 31.4x forward earnings, a fair valuation, in my view, considering the opportunities ahead. The stock may not stay down for too long. Investors should buy the dip.

    Microsoft Stock Gave Back 8% Within 2 Weeks of Its Record. Here's How Past Quick Pullbacks Like This Played Out.

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (878 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that microsoft (MSFT -2.77%) hit a record close of $555.80 on Nov.
    • Part of that drop comes from the broader market.
    • It has been revealed that A fast drop from a upcoming peak can feel like a warning.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 22, 2026 at 3:41AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Microsoft ›.

    It has been revealed that microsoft (MSFT -2.77%) hit a record close of $555.80 on Nov. 4. Nine trading days later, on Nov. 17, it ended at $506.24 -- around 9% under the high. Shares trade near $508 as of this writing.

    Part of that drop comes from the broader market. The Nasdaq-100 fell around 5% in the same stretch. But Microsoft fell more.

    It has been revealed that A fast drop from a upcoming peak can feel like a warning. For Microsoft, it usually hasn't been one.

    By my count of its daily closes, the stock has fallen this fast from a record on 18 past occasions since 1995. Shares were higher 12 months later in 15 of the cases, and the typical (median) gain was around 30%. That's about twice the median one-year gain of about 15% for all trading days in the same stretch.

    According to recent reports, every case begins on the first day Microsoft closed at least 8% under a record close set within the past 15 trading days. I used split-adjusted closing prices without dividends and counted just one case per record, so a stock that kept falling couldn't count twice until it hit a new high.

    "A year later" means the close 12 months after that first 8% day.

    According to recent reports, the recent record is especially strong. Since 2018, Microsoft has done this nine times, and the stock was higher a year later in all nine. The middle result was a rise of around 29%.

    The best one came in September 2020, when shares rose about 48% over the next year.

    Recent findings suggest that but the ride was rarely smooth. Ten of the 18 saw shares fall at least another 10% before the year ended.

    The latest case shows how rough that can be. Once the stock slid 8% under its Oct. 28, 2025, record, it eventually closed around 29% below where it stood on that 8% day. It didn't hit a new record until Oct. 13, 2026. And a year after the pullback started, it was up only about 7%.

    The three cases that finished lower fell within around nine months of each other, in April 1999, July 1999, and January 2000. A year later, shares were down each time, by up to about 50%.

    The last one was by far the worst. Microsoft set a record close on Dec. 27, 1999, and fell 8% under it in January 2000. It didn't close above its 1999 high again until October 2016 -- almost 17 years later.

    One substantial difference between then and now is valuation. In all three cases, the stock cost more than 60 times the earnings Microsoft had reported in the previous four quarters.

    In a recent development, today, Microsoft's non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings for its past four quarters are $18.04 per share, a number that leaves out the impact of its investments in OpenAI. The stock trades at around 28 times those earnings.

    True, the stock arguably still has a premium price for a tech business this big. But it's nowhere near the multiples investors paid then.

    Of course, earnings growth has cooled a little. Adjusted earnings per share climbed 18% year over year in Microsoft's fiscal first quarter of 2027 (the period ended Sept. 30, 2026). That was its slowest rate in at least four quarters, after growth between 21% and 24% in the previous three quarters.

    Recent findings suggest that what makes this case unusual is that Microsoft's Nov. 4 record came on a one-day jump of almost 7%. None of the 18 past records in this study came on a one-day gain larger than about 5%.

    In a recent development, so a lot of the latest drop has just given that jump back. Measured from its Nov. 3 close of around $521, the stock is down only about 2%. In other words, the drop from the record likely overstates how much has changed for Microsoft since early November.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Industry observers note that all in all, the record here looks promising for long-term shareholders. A quick 8% slide from a high has usually been followed by gains, and the exceptions were when the stock was priced well above where it is now.

    But I don't see a reason to rush. More than half the time, buyers had a chance to pay at least 10% less at some point during the year.

    And with earnings growth slowing and the stock still about 28 times adjusted earnings, I'd rather wait for a lower price than the one offered now.

    If this pullback follows most of the others, that chance might come -- but history isn't a guarantee.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • One of the few bright spots in the crypto market has been Hyperliquid (HYPE +5.86%), up 140% for the year.
    • It has been revealed that but can Hyperliquid hold on to these gains and surge even higher in the years ahead?
    • First and foremost, Hyperliquid still faces tremendous regulatory obstacles.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Dominic Basulto – Nov 22, 2026 at 4:00AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Hyperliquid ›.

    One of the few bright spots in the crypto market has been Hyperliquid (HYPE +5.86%), up 140% for the year. Since its launch in late 2024, the HYPE token is up a remarkable 1,800%.

    It has been revealed that but can Hyperliquid hold on to these gains and surge even higher in the years ahead? If so, it could be a millionaire maker. But before you start shopping for luxury yachts and high-end vacation homes, here's what you need to know about Hyperliquid.

    First and foremost, Hyperliquid still faces tremendous regulatory obstacles. That's because Hyperliquid is a decentralized crypto exchange based offshore, and it doesn't yet have regulatory permission to operate in the U.S. or to offer its services to U.S. retail investors. If you try to trade on the Hyperliquid platform, you will immediately get a red warning message that you're in a restricted jurisdiction.

    Industry observers note that granted, President Donald Trump has given regulators the green light to bring Hyperliquid to the U.S. That's a huge positive. But the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) recently warned that Hyperliquid would be treated just like any other entity. Until it receives formal regulatory approval, Hyperliquid will need to partner with a registered exchange to offer financial derivatives to U.S. retail investors.

    Meanwhile, the number of participants lining up to offer perpetual futures -- the financial product that led to Hyperliquid's meteoric rise -- seems to increase by the day. That's because the CFTC gave the go-ahead for crypto perps in May and for equity perps in November, which has dramatically changed the competitive landscape.

    It's not just decentralized exchanges such as Hyperliquid that are potential rivals. Centralized crypto exchanges such as Coinbase Global (COIN -6.34%) and trading platforms like Robinhood Markets (HOOD -9.44%) are also potential rivals. So are prediction markets such as Kalshi and Polymarket. And what if legacy Wall Street financial exchanges decide to get into the act?

    You get the idea. Competition could be off the charts, and that means Hyperliquid may start to account for a shrinking share of trading in perpetual futures. If that's the case, there's no way that it can grow at triple-digit percentage rates in coming years.

    Sources indicate that and here's the really scary fact: Hyperliquid is now down 37% from its all-time high of $97.98 in September. If roughly $100 were the top for HYPE, it wouldn't surprise me at all. In the crypto market, it's normal for highly volatile cryptos to skyrocket in price one year, only to collapse the next.

    All of this is to say: Don't believe the hype about HYPE.

    Given that almost all cryptocurrencies are down this year, it's easy to suspend disbelief and think that Hyperliquid might be a magic ticket to millionaire status. But I just don't think it has the staying power required to mint latest millionaires. Hyperliquid might be beating the pants off Bitcoin (BTC +3.93%) this year, but I'd still rather buy Bitcoin.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.
    • According to recent reports, here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept.
    • Recent findings suggest that robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.

    According to recent reports, here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

    Recent findings suggest that robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

    Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

    Robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly important sources of transaction revenue, while the firm has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

    Transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

    Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

    Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

    Net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

    —With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney.

    Industry News: Is a Stock Market Crash Imminent for the AI-Driven Trump Bull Market? History Weighs In With an Unpleasant Answer.

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (900 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, although some of Wall Street's most volatile single-session swings in history have occurred under President Donald Trump, few presidents since the late 1890s have overseen higher average annual stock market returns.
    • The stock market's list of catalysts under Trump is extensive and includes (but isn't limited to):.
    • Industry observers note that president Trump's bull market may be operating on borrowed time.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Sean Williams – Nov 22, 2026 at 4:06AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    According to recent reports, although some of Wall Street's most volatile single-session swings in history have occurred under President Donald Trump, few presidents since the late 1890s have overseen higher average annual stock market returns. During Trump's first term, the time-tested Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI -1.93%), benchmark S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%), and innovation-powered Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -5.28%) gained 57%, 70%, and 142%, respectively.

    The stock market's list of catalysts under Trump is extensive and includes (but isn't limited to):.

    Industry observers note that president Trump's bull market may be operating on borrowed time. Image source: Official White House Photo by Daniel Torok.

    Industry observers note that but things may not be as ideal for Wall Street as the major stock indexes have made them appear. History suggests the probability of a stock market crash occurring and driving the AI-driven Trump bull market notably lower is climbing by the day.

    There's no argument that AI is the hottest trend on Wall Street since the advent and proliferation of the internet. Empowering software and systems to make autonomous decisions is a $22.5 trillion addressable opportunity through 2031, according to IDC, and it's the primary catalyst that's lifted the Trump bull market to latest heights.

    But history also reveals that every next-big-thing technology since (and including) the advent of the internet in the mid-1990s has navigated a bubble-bursting event. These bubbles repeatedly form and burst because investors persistently overestimate the pace of adoption and/or optimization of latest technologies.

    Recent findings suggest that stock market bubbles throughout history…AI stocks now ~40% of the market. pic.twitter.com/RxSAh09k6F.

    To be clear, AI doesn't have an adoption problem. The amount of capital being thrown around by neoclouds and hyperscalers shows that AI has been welcomed with open arms.

    However, the businesses deploying AI solutions aren't particularly close to optimizing them. It took until several years after the dot-com bubble burst for internet-driven companies to maximize this technology to boost their sales and profits, and we're likely looking at a similar timeline for AI, heightening the odds of a bubble-driven stock market crash.

    Premium stock valuations are another reason the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite could endure elevator-down moves in the presumed not-too-distant future.

    On the one hand, valuation is a tricky subject to tackle given that there isn't a one-size-fits-all way to evaluate individual companies or the broader market. Some combination of investor subjectivity and emotion leads to unpredictability on Wall Street.

    Stock Market Shiller PE Ratio on the verge of taking out its Dot Com Bubble all-time high 🚨 🤯 👀 pic.twitter.com/CtCmSgWnLt.

    It has been revealed that on the other hand, the S&P 500's Shiller Price-to-Earnings (P/E) Ratio, also known as the Cyclically Adjusted P/E Ratio (CAPE Ratio), is time-vetted and leaves little room for interpretation. The stock market entered this year at its second-highest valuation since January 1871 and only became more expensive throughout the summer.

    In a recent development, the S&P 500's CAPE Ratio has exceeded 30 only six times over 156 years, including the present, and the previous five instances were all eventually followed by declines of 20% to 89% in the Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500, and/or Nasdaq Composite. While the Shiller P/E Ratio doesn't tell investors when these downturns will begin or if a crash will occur, it does have a knack for foreshadowing substantial downside.

    Wall Street's crudest measure of investors' willingness to take risks also points to a heightened probability of a stock market crash.

    Sources indicate that every month, FINRA publishes the aggregated outstanding margin debt at all brokerages. Margin represents the money investors borrow, with interest, to short-sell or purchase securities. When it's used to buy stocks or exchange-traded funds, it acts as leverage.

    Industry observers note that investing on margin can be incredibly risky. It can magnify your gains if a security moves in the desired direction, but also quickly amplify losses if it moves in the opposite direction.

    Total Margin Debt hits $1.5 Trillion, a fresh all-time high 🤯 👀 pic.twitter.com/1IXqZGgrqs.

    In June 2026, outstanding margin debt hit a record high of $1.502 trillion. While margin debt is expected to steadily climb with the overall stock market over time, parabolic moves higher over short time frames have historically been bad news. Between April 2025 and June 2026, margin debt soared 77%, marking the fourth time it's skyrocketed by at least 65% since 1998 over the span of just 12 to 19 months.

    The prior three occurrences immediately preceded the bursting of the dot-com bubble in 2000, the start of the financial crisis in 2007, and the onset of the 2022 bear market. Some of these events featured crash-like moves.

    While none of these three history-backed events or metrics guarantee that a Trump bull market crash is imminent, the odds of a jaw-dropping downturn appear to be growing by the day.

    10 stocks we like better than Eli Lilly ›.

    Eli Lilly (LLY -0.30%) is a well-established pharmaceutical company, known for delivering reliable revenue year after year. Patients need their medicines regardless of the economic backdrop, and this fact offers pharma giants a certain amount of stability. This translates into an element of safety for investors.

    But Eli Lilly also offers something that many of us associate with other industries, such as technology. I'm talking about growth. The organization has generated double-digit revenue gains in recent quarters thanks to its presence in the weight loss drug space. Lilly sells tirzepatide under the names Mounjaro for type 2 diabetes and Zepbound for weight loss. (Doctors have prescribed either one for the weight loss indication.).

    In a recent development, all of this helped the stock climb more than 420% over the past five years, meaning that if you invested $1,000, you would have over $5,000 today. Could it soar that much again by 2031? Let's find out.

    According to recent reports, so, first, let's take a look at Eli Lilly's path over the past few years. This pharma giant sells a broad range of medicines across treatment areas, from cancer to migraine and Alzheimer's disease. But the area that has stood out in recent years is weight loss. Lilly's drugs are in the class known as GLP-1. These drugs act on hormonal pathways involved in digestion and therefore regulate appetite and blood sugar levels.

    Sources indicate that individuals aiming to lose weight have rushed to get in on GLP-1 drugs since they've proven safety and efficacy and are easy to self-administer. Mounjaro and Zepbound are weekly injections, and Lilly recently won approval for a newly introduced GLP-1 drug in pill format. That product is called Foundayo and may significantly broaden the audience for these types of drugs.

    It has been revealed that lilly isn't alone in the market; in fact, it wasn't even the leader in the early days of GLP-1 drugs. Novo Nordisk was the original leader, though Lilly slipped ahead in 2025. Now, the two are vying for leadership in the oral GLP-1 space, as Novo also introduced an oral drug this year.

    Lilly's recent earnings report demonstrates the power of its GLP-1 drugs, with Mounjaro and Zepbound driving a 39% increase in revenue to more than $24 billion.

    The story doesn't end here, though. Lilly also has an extensive pipeline of weight loss drug candidates, including one called retatrutide that's in phase 3 studies and may have the potential to deliver greater weight loss. This could complement the existing portfolio, offering a variety of GLP-1 options for different needs.

    Now, let's consider whether an investment in Lilly could once again turn $1,000 into $5,000 over the coming five years. This would imply a gain of about 420%, taking the share price to about $7,092 -- and the market cap from $1.2 trillion today to $6.3 trillion. This surpasses the value of today's biggest technology leaders.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    In a recent development, of course, it's possible that over the coming five years, tech players also will gain, seeing their market values march higher. So the market as a whole may see value climb significantly, making the Lilly jump to more than $6 trillion seem less shocking.

    That mentioned, after the S&P 500's 78% increase over the past three calendar years and the double- and triple-digit gains of many massive stocks, I wouldn't count on the same momentum over the coming five years -- for the general market or for Lilly. This doesn't mean the market or Lilly will drop. I think there's still potential for gains, and Lilly's weight loss portfolio and potentially new debuts from the pipeline could drive significant growth.

    Though I would be surprised to see another gain of 400%, I think it's possible to see a double- or triple-digit increase from Lilly stock over the next five years -- and that means I consider it a great buy today.

    Breaking: Medicare Open Enrollment Will Soon Be Over: 3 Things to Do ASAP if You Haven't Done Them Already

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (558 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that if you're enrolled in Medicare, there's an vital deadline approaching that could affect how much you pay for healthcare next year.
    • In a recent development, even if you're satisfied with your current Medicare proposal, assuming everything will remain the same and there's no better option out there could be a costly mistake.
    • Open enrollment gives you an opportunity to make changes to your Medicare coverage.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Maurie Backman – Nov 22, 2026 at 4:18AM EST.

    Sources indicate that if you're enrolled in Medicare, there's an vital deadline approaching that could affect how much you pay for healthcare next year. Medicare's fall open enrollment period ends on Dec. 7. That means you only have a limited amount of time to review your coverage and make changes for 2027.

    In a recent development, even if you're satisfied with your current Medicare proposal, assuming everything will remain the same and there's no better option out there could be a costly mistake. So make sure to do these three things before the Dec. 7 deadline arrives.

    Open enrollment gives you an opportunity to make changes to your Medicare coverage. But before you can decide whether a new plan is best, you have to understand what's happening with your current one.

    According to recent reports, to that end, if you haven't reviewed your current strategy's annual notice of change, now's the time to read through it thoroughly. That notice should explain any upcoming changes to things like premiums, deductibles, copays, covered services, and other benefits.

    Don't just skim that document, though. Even a relatively small monthly premium increase could add up over the course of a year. And if your Medicare Advantage plan is dropping benefits, that could have a huge impact on you, too.

    According to recent reports, before comparing Medicare prepares, take the time to make a list of every prescription medication you currently take. Include the medication's name, dosage, how frequently you take it, and the pharmacy you typically use for refills.

    This step is notable because Medicare Part D plans can change their drug formularies, which are lists of covered prescription medications, from one year to the next. A medication covered by your current proposal might be moved to a different cost-sharing tier in 2027, making it more expensive. Having a comprehensive list should make it easier to compare plans and determine which one offers the best coverage for your specific medications.

    Industry observers note that even if your current Medicare plan isn't changing for the worse, you shouldn't assume that it's your best option for next year. There may be another plan that offers lower premiums and prescription drug costs.

    It has been revealed that if you've been diagnosed with any new conditions over the past year, it also pays to see if there's a Medicare Advantage blueprint offering supplemental benefits that could help you manage it better. Medicare Advantage plans commonly offer added benefits beyond what original Medicare covers.

    According to recent reports, it might seem like you have plenty of time to take action on your Medicare coverage before Dec. 7 rolls around. But that deadline will be here before you know it. So if you haven't yet reviewed changes to your current Medicare strategy, your prescription list, and upcoming plan options, the time to get moving is now.

    Tech Report: Broadcom Stock Is 27% Below Its June Record. Here's Where I Think It Will Be in 2030.

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (857 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that broadcom (AVGO -12.19%) shares trade around $353 as I write this, about 27% below the record $481.57 they closed at on June 2.
    • It has been revealed that I think it could hit around $600.
    • Recent findings suggest that this estimate hinges on one earnings path, based mainly on Broadcom's artificial intelligence (AI) chips, and one ending valuation.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 22, 2026 at 4:19AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Broadcom ›.

    It has been revealed that broadcom (AVGO -12.19%) shares trade around $353 as I write this, about 27% below the record $481.57 they closed at on June 2. But in the quarter Broadcom reported in September, the chip designer's non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings per share surged 96% from a year earlier.

    Where could Broadcom stock be by the end of 2030?

    It has been revealed that I think it could hit around $600. That'd be a rise of about 70% from today's price, or about 14% a year.

    Recent findings suggest that this estimate hinges on one earnings path, based mainly on Broadcom's artificial intelligence (AI) chips, and one ending valuation. It also comes before the company's fiscal fourth-quarter report on Dec. 9, which might change both.

    And it relies most on one assumption: that a really short list of customers keeps buying.

    Sources indicate that showing how fast the AI business is scaling, Broadcom's AI semiconductor revenue climbed 221% year over year to $16.7 billion in the fiscal third quarter of 2026 (the period ended Aug. 2, 2026). Management sees fiscal Q4 AI revenue of $21.7 billion, an acceleration to 236% growth, which would take the fiscal 2026 total to about $58 billion. Custom AI chips, which Broadcom designs for specific customers, made up 73% of the third-quarter total. And AI networking revenue, from the chips that tie those processors together, climbed over 2.5-fold from a year earlier.

    In a recent development, management also said on its September earnings call that it's locked in the supply to double AI revenue again in fiscal 2027, to about $115 billion. It sees a path to $230 billion in fiscal 2028, and it expects networking to grow just as fast as the custom chips.

    "As a result, I got to say we are very much on target to exceed $30 in earnings per share in fiscal 2028," CEO Hock Tan noted on the call.

    I use that $30 as my base for fiscal 2028. Then, I assume earnings growth slows to around 10% a year as the largest data center build-outs mature. This would put earnings per share at about $40 in fiscal 2031.

    It has been revealed that today, the stock price is around 18 times the fiscal 2027 earnings per share analysts expect on average. The S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) traded at about 18 times forward earnings in mid-November, according to FactSet.

    Sure, Broadcom is growing far faster than the index now. By the end of 2030, though, investors will probably be pricing the stock on fiscal 2031 earnings, and growth should be much slower. So I assume a lower price-to-earnings ratio of around 15.

    At 15 times forward earnings of about $40, the stock would be worth about $600.

    That means all the gain in my estimate comes from earnings growth, with investors paying less for every dollar of Broadcom's profit than they do now.

    Sources indicate that profitability looks like a smaller risk. Management expects adjusted gross margin to ease to around 73% in fiscal Q4, from 78% a year earlier, as memory-heavy custom chips grow. But it sees the adjusted operating margin staying at about 66%, flat year over year.

    Sources indicate that the bigger risk is who buys those chips. Broadcom estimates that its top five end customers made up around 55% of its fiscal third-quarter revenue, versus about 40% a year earlier. In the first three quarters of fiscal 2026, that share was about 50%.

    Recent findings suggest that broadcom makes custom AI chips for six customers. Management expects Anthropic to become the largest of them in 2027, and OpenAI the second largest in 2028.

    The company's latest quarterly filing warns that losing any top-five customer, or a big fall in demand from one, could have a material adverse effect on its business.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Industry observers note that what if the significant deployments are around two years late? Then earnings per share might hit $30 in fiscal 2030 and about $33 in fiscal 2031. At the same 15 times forward earnings, the stock would land near $500 instead, for yearly gains of about 9%.

    That's still a decent return. But a customer that stops buying entirely could do much more harm.

    All in all, I think around $600 is a fair estimate for Broadcom stock at the end of 2030. If those customers keep building, today's price looks reasonable to me for a firm with that path ahead of it. But that's just a guess, and much of it rests on spending decisions Broadcom doesn't control.

    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    The Stock Market Sounds an Alarm as Investors Get Bad News About President Donald Trump's Economy

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (790 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) and Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -5.28%) delivered positive returns for much of 2026, supported by strong corporate earnings and enthusiasm surrounding artificial intelligence.
    • According to recent reports, unfortunately, the situation could get worse.
    • President Donald Trump sits with his hands clasped during a meeting at the White House, surrounded by administration officials.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Trevor Jennewine – Nov 22, 2026 at 4:21AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    According to recent reports, the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) and Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -5.28%) delivered positive returns for much of 2026, supported by strong corporate earnings and enthusiasm surrounding artificial intelligence. But both indexes recently entered market correction territory, falling more than 10% from their respective highs.

    According to recent reports, unfortunately, the situation could get worse. Investors recently received troubling updates about President Donald Trump's economy: Inflation accelerated in September, and subsequent estimates suggest pricing pressures have continued to intensify. Meanwhile, the stock market is sounding an alarm last seen during the dot-com bubble.

    Here's what investors should know.

    President Donald Trump sits with his hands clasped during a meeting at the White House, surrounded by administration officials. Image source: Official White House Photo.

    Recent findings suggest that inflation accelerated in September, complicating the Federal Reserve's effort to restore price stability. The Consumer Price Index (CPI) increased 3.7% from the previous year, up from 3.4% in August and the highest reading since May.

    Research from the Federal Reserve Banks of St. Louis and Minneapolis helps explain why prices are rising more rapidly. President Trump's tariffs were the primary driver of inflation earlier in the year, but supply shocks driven by energy sector prices have since become the primary culprit. The Iran war has disrupted Middle Eastern oil shipments, pushing crude oil prices and transportation costs higher.

    Unfortunately, the inflation outlook remains troubling. The Cleveland Fed estimates that headline CPI inflation is trending toward 3.9% in November. And core CPI inflation (which excludes volatile food and energy prices) is projected to accelerate to 2.9%, up from 2.6% in September, suggesting that elevated energy prices are spreading to other areas of the economy.

    The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate in September, the first rate hike in three years, but investors expect another rate hike in December due to persistent inflation. That bodes ill for the stock market because higher interest rates increase borrowing costs for consumers and businesses, potentially slowing economic growth and creating a drag on corporate profits. They also make bonds more attractive relative to stocks, which can put downward pressure on equity valuations.

    The price-to-earnings (PE) ratio is one of the most widely used equity valuation metrics. It divides a tech giant's share price by its earnings per share from the last 12 months. But the cyclically adjusted price-to-earnings (CAPE) ratio takes a different approach, dividing the inflation-adjusted price by the average inflation-adjusted earnings from the last decade. That methodology smooths fluctuations in corporate profits caused by the business cycle.

    Sources indicate that the S&P 500's CAPE ratio was 40.1 in October, marking the sixth straight monthly reading above 40. Previously, the index's CAPE ratio last exceeded 40 during the dot-com crash in September 2000. Unfortunately, such rich valuations have often preceded dismal returns, as shown in the table below.

    Data source: Robert Shiller, YCharts.

    Historically, following months in which the S&P 500's CAPE ratio exceeded 40, the index returned an average of 0% over the next six months; it declined by an average of 3% over the next year; and it declined by an average of 19% over the next two years. In other words, history suggests the stock market is headed much lower.

    It has been revealed that however, one limitation of the CAPE ratio is its backward-looking nature. It does not incorporate forward earnings estimates, meaning it may overstate valuations when corporate profits are growing quickly. Artificial intelligence has already contributed to higher profit margins and higher earnings growth across the S&P 500, and that trend is projected to continue.

    Additionally, the historical returns shown in the table reflect overlapping periods during the dot-com bubble, rather than numerous independent market episodes. Consequently, they illustrate the risks associated with extreme valuations, but do not definitively predict what will happen next.

    Nevertheless, investors should not dismiss this warning entirely The stock market remains expensive by historical standards, and the prospect of higher interest rates could put additional pressure on valuations. Together, those headwinds could push the S&P 500 into a bear market. If that happens, remember that dips have historically been great buying opportunities: The S&P 500 has rebounded from every past drawdown.

    Where Will Micron Stock Be in 3 Years?

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Micron Technology (MU -13.89%) has lost nearly half its market cap in five months.
    • Wall Street thinks that Micron has a lot of room to run.
    • The bull case for Micron is that its stock soars to between $1,800 and $2,200 by late 2029, a gain of 3.2x at the midpoint of the range.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Keith Speights – Nov 22, 2026 at 4:26AM EST.

    Micron Technology (MU -13.89%) has lost nearly half its market cap in five months. That's the bad news. The good news is that the semiconductor stock is still up nearly 120% year-to-date.

    Wall Street thinks that Micron has a lot of room to run. The consensus 12-month price target reflects a potential upside of around 160%. But where will Micron stock be in three years? There are three potential scenarios.

    The bull case for Micron is that its stock soars to between $1,800 and $2,200 by late 2029, a gain of 3.2x at the midpoint of the range. To make this scenario possible, the demand for the company's memory chips would need to remain strong over the next several years. In addition, the humanoid robot market would need to gain momentum. Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra mentioned in the company's fiscal 2026 third-quarter earnings call that he expects a "sustained, substantial multi-decade memory demand cycle" to begin later this decade.

    The base case is that the stock jumps to $1,100 to $1,400. Micron's share price would roughly double at the midpoint of this range. The high-bandwidth memory (HBM) market would need to continue growing robustly in this scenario. It also assumes that Chinese memory chip manufacturer ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) gains only modest market share with its HBM chips. However, Micron probably wouldn't require the humanoid robot market to pick up significant steam for the base case to be achieved.

    In a recent development, what's the bear case? Micron's stock declines to a range of $400 to $600 over the next three years. The most likely way this scenario could unfold is if CXMT advances its HBM technology faster than expected and changes the market dynamics. An influx of HBM supply could trigger a price war among major HBM suppliers. As Micron's margins fall, so would its share price. A slowdown in AI infrastructure spending could also weigh on Micron's stock. With many investors already nervous about hyperscalers' massive AI-related capital expenditures and a growing public backlash against AI data centers in the U.S., such a slowdown isn't out of the question.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Micron is still a cyclical stock. Any of the three scenarios is possible, depending on the duration and intensity of the current memory chip boom. That said, if I had to predict where Micron stock will actually be three years from now, it would be around the lower end of the base-case range.

    In a recent development, I fully expect the demand for HBM to remain strong. Whether the humanoid robot market becomes a significant tailwind for Micron between now and 2029 remains to be seen, though. As for CXMT, I think the organization will be a key player in HBM. However, I don't anticipate that Micron's growth will be derailed because of increased competition. A cumulative gain of 80% or more for Micron over the next three years seems attainable, in my view.

    #96570. What Every 60-Year-Old Should Know About Social Security

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (692 w)
